blueprint_topic: Management of Care — infectious-diseases review and discharge coordination before OPAT
stem: A hospitalized client is clinically stable and is being prepared for discharge to complete antimicrobial treatment through outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT). Which action should the RN prioritize during discharge coordination?

options.A: Verify that an infectious-diseases expert has reviewed the antimicrobial plan before OPAT is initiated.
options.B: Finalize the existing parenteral regimen once home-infusion services are available and obtain infectious-diseases input at the first outpatient follow-up.
options.C: Continue the inpatient parenteral regimen after discharge when the client is improving and defer route reassessment until the planned course is completed.
options.D: Base readiness for OPAT on vascular-access and self-administration planning, with infectious-diseases review reserved for treatment complications.

rationale: A is correct. IDSA Recommendation 17 states that all patients should have infectious-diseases expert review before initiation of OPAT (strong recommendation, very low-quality evidence). The guideline's rationale notes that expert review can identify unnecessary OPAT, an appropriate oral regimen, or situations in which antimicrobial therapy should be modified. B is incorrect because it postpones the recommended expert review until after OPAT has begun. C is incorrect because clinical improvement does not make the inpatient parenteral route automatically appropriate for outpatient continuation; the pre-OPAT review is intended in part to reassess whether parenteral therapy remains necessary. D is incorrect because vascular-access and administration logistics are important OPAT considerations but do not replace the recommended infectious-diseases expert review before initiation.
educational_objective: Before OPAT begins, coordinate infectious-diseases expert review of the antimicrobial plan so the need for parenteral therapy, antimicrobial selection, and outpatient treatment plan are reassessed before discharge implementation.
source_document_title: IDSA 2018 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Outpatient Parenteral Antimicrobial Therapy
source_version_date: Published November 13, 2018; listed as Current on the IDSA Practice Guidelines A-Z page when rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: Antimicrobial Stewardship — Question XVII, Recommendation 17: all patients should have infectious-diseases expert review prior to initiation of OPAT (strong recommendation, very low-quality evidence). Rationale: ID expert review may curtail unnecessary OPAT and identify patients for whom oral or no antimicrobial therapy is appropriate or for whom the antimicrobial plan should be modified. IDSA Practice Guidelines A-Z: Outpatient Parenteral Antimicrobial Therapy 2018 is listed as Current.
source_claim_supported: Current IDSA OPAT guidance recommends infectious-diseases expert review before OPAT initiation, in part to reassess whether parenteral therapy and the selected antimicrobial plan are appropriate.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care, printed page 7/PDF page 11: 'Identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members when providing client care'; 'Assess the need for referrals and obtain necessary orders'; 'Recognize limitations of self and others and utilize resources'; 'Provide care within the legal scope of practice.'
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan printed page 7/PDF page 11 visually verified by screenshot on 2026-08-20; no CACHE MISS.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'OPAT infectious-diseases expert review' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the OPAT care-coordination construct and key A, but rebuilt distractors to remove must/all-style cueing and replace obviously implausible alternatives with realistic timing, route-reassessment, and logistics-versus-specialist-review errors.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches IDSA Recommendation 17 and is appropriate RN discharge-coordination behavior.
option_audit.B: Plausible timing error; incorrect because it moves ID expert review to after OPAT initiation.
option_audit.C: Plausible continuity-of-therapy error; incorrect because improvement alone does not eliminate the recommended pre-OPAT expert reassessment of route and regimen.
option_audit.D: Plausible logistics-focused error; incorrect because access and administration readiness do not substitute for pre-initiation ID expert review.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/must/all-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: The correct response is concise but not uniquely signaled by length; distractors contain comparable clinical detail.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All options are parallel discharge-coordination actions and remain within the same construct.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified: B, C, and D each conflict with the explicit timing and purpose of IDSA Recommendation 17.
